items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: and of course, played on a recording with Fats

ctx.x: But I used to listen to all of his records because, and incidentally, found out about these records through Bix because Bix told us about Ethel Waters and as you know, Lucky Roberts made all the Ethel Waters records, so but I never heard him play, in person.

But I heard James P., and in fact, I did a couple of concerts with James P. in New York, one of those Condon series things, and of course, played on a recording with Fats and never recorded with Earl Hines, but played -- did a long tour of

28 straight days with a band several years ago here in the U.K. called -- well, the band was from they were bands from the States and it was called Jazz of the Swing Era, but I have known Earl since I was a kid, because when Earl -- Earl joined Louis at the Sunset, say in 1925 or '26, I used to go there three or four nights a week to hear Earl and Louis. 'Cause This was a couple years after the King Oliver thing.
